title: Fix the ringed one: one typed second go, and the ring wears a tick
body:
## Summary
On Math Buddy's Walk, a ringed item is a dead end: the pen shows where it broke and the learner can do nothing with that on the desk. Give a wrong item ONE typed second go on the phone; code judges it, the TV draws the result as a picture (the ring now wears a tick) and the record keeps the honest first attempt.

## Description
Today the loop after a slip is: look where the pen is, rework on paper, then either press Six more (a brand new set; the same question never returns) or describe it by voice, which can only rename the slip. The desk never learns that the learner fixed it, and the learner never learns whether the fix holds. Essay Master already closes this loop for sentences (rewrite in place, the move inks, a ghost arrow shows the before and after); Math Buddy, whose whole pitch is that the pen shows the line, does not.

The data and the judge are already there. `typedSettle` judges one typed answer for every item kind with no model call; the item carries its slip and pen position; the Lamplight vocabulary already has the ring and the earned tick. The move: a wrong item with no second go may take one typed answer from the phone (`POST /api/second`, `{n, answer}`); code decides (`typedSettle`), an unreadable answer is refused in a desk sentence and does not spend the go; the route raises one server-only event `practice.second {n, verdict}`, which carries a verdict and never the typed answer; the reducer sets `second: 'right' | 'wrong'` once and leaves verdict, slip, pen, history, digest and the learner record exactly as marking wrote them (a second go is practice, not evidence, the same ruling `reviseSentence` makes for essays).

On the TV nothing asks for typing and nothing new is said: on the Sheet and the Walk a fixed item keeps its ring and pen (the record of where it broke) and gains the earned orange tick on its number and its tally mark; a second go that missed draws a second ring stroke. The taped card carries one short sentence in the same slot. 'To look at' counts and the first-to-look focus skip a fixed item; Tonight's hero, the landing and the recap keep reading the first attempt, so the record and every summary agree.

## Flow
- Walk on a ringed item: phone shows 'Try it again' (one box, one Send) under the voice prompt, only for a wrong item with no second go.
- Send -> `/api/second` -> `secondProblem(item)` -> `typedSettle` -> `practice.second` -> the TV redraws: ring plus tick, or a double ring.
- Back to the sheet: the head reads 'One to look at' instead of 'Two'; focus lands on the next unfixed item.
- Six more still works as before.

## Expected impact
The single most common thing a child does after a marked set (go back to the line and fix it) becomes visible: 4 steps and a lost question become 1 typed answer and one picture, inside the same Walk. It adds the missing half of the pen's promise without a point, a streak or a percentage, never puts an answer or a verdict word on the phone, and the one-go limit keeps it from becoming guess-and-check.

## Evaluation
Claim: a wrong item takes one code-judged typed second go, drawn as a picture, with the record untouched.
Before: 0 of 7 behaviour cases pass (case 8 is a declared GUARD, green before by design); a wrong item has no road to be answered again (store.ts:525-528, explain.ts:177-181).
After: 7 of 7 behaviour cases pass and the guard stays green; the existing tv-sheet, maths-tv, maths-rules, school-marking and phone-panel suites unchanged and green.
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: direction (the map's description names the marked sheet and its walk, not a second go; it falls inside STUDY-DESK-SCOPE.md's Check my work, overturned 2026-09-08). Contract consumers of the new item field and event: store.ts (type, shown, reducer, NEEDS_LEARNER), api/session/route.ts (SERVER_ONLY), tv/sheetRows.ts, maths/MathsTV.tsx, app/phone/page.tsx; not touched by design: memory.ts, rules/digest.ts, tv/landingRows.ts, tv/screens.tsx recap (they read the first attempt).
evidence: store.ts:525-528 reducer: `shown(e.verdict && it.verdict === "unsure" ? {...} : !e.verdict && e.slip && it.verdict === "wrong" && slipsFor(topic).some(...) ? { ...it, slip, said, reply } : { ...it, reply })` - a wrong item can take a slip name or a reply, never a verdict. explain.ts:177-181 comment: 'renamed is set only when the item was already wrong ... Its verdict, its pen (slipAt) and the learner record are left as they were.' working.ts:58-62 lookAt returns 'Look where the pen is.' for a slipAt-placed wrong item. phone/page.tsx:459 `asking = !!item && (item.verdict === "wrong" || item.verdict === "unsure" || !!reply)` gates only the voice box. Steps today to learn whether a correction holds: finish the Walk, Back to the sheet, Down to Six more, Select, wait for a new set (school units are code-written, linear sets are a model call), work six NEW questions, snap or type, wait for marking = 6+ steps and the corrected question is gone; after: type one answer on the phone, read one picture. Four TV-side derivations of the same tally: sheetRows.ts:32, MathsTV.tsx:476, 775, 777. probe context: `typedSettle` is the proven single-item judge (maths school-marking-test.cjs test 11 pins typed == photo for school sets); mark.ts:332 already drops the pen for a typed answer, which is why the second go keeps the first attempt's pen. Never-re-propose check: challenge-2026-09-25 desk-pipelines B ('Rewrite one sentence in place') is Essay only; challenge-2026-09-25 desk-pipelines A moved pen location into rules/maths and did not add an answer-again road; no finding in the prior findings.jsonl titles mentions a second go. Hot files: store.ts is in the write set (one field, one event, one case); tv/keys.ts, tv/screens.tsx and uat/driver/linga-text.cjs are not (no new key: the TV never asks for typing). Wave note: card A rewrites mark.ts and rules go through kinds.ts; run A first, then B imports judgeItem instead of exporting typedSettle (B's mark.ts hunk is one export line and disappears).

title: One owner for the phone, and one table for the level check
body:
## Summary
The phone and the TV can be in two different Linga activities at once, and the phone obeys the wrong one. A level check that was left (stop, Not now, Esc, or just choosing a situation from the menu) is kept forever, and while it is kept the phone shows the check instead of the rehearsal the TV is running. The learner speaks to Jamie and the phone sends it to the level check; on the topic question that reply becomes their stored goal. The conversation got a turn table in the last challenge; the level check, which has the same shape of loose fields, did not, and nothing decides which of the two owns the desk.

## Description
Two session slots, s.conversation and s.check, both persist and both can be live. Seven places pick the owner by hand and every one of them picks the check first (view.ts:170-178, 186-189, 196-208, 531-535; LingaTV.tsx:26, 47-55; LingaPhone.tsx:22, 62-64). Only three commands ever clear a check (level-self, plan-agree, a learner change), so a check abandoned at any stage outlives every scene started after it. Starting a scene never looks at the check (conversation.ts:128-148) and resuming one never does (conversation.ts:160). The result, shown by a probe against the real modules: with the TV on a rehearsal, the phone's answer is plan-goal (the reply is saved as preferences.goal and lost to the conversation) or check-answer (the reply is judged as a level-check answer).

The move is one small module, activity.ts, with two parts, both pure and imported by the server, the view, the TV and the phone exactly as turn.ts is. First, ownerOf(session): which of check, conversation or neither holds the phone now, decided once. A check is parked (a new optional LevelCheck.parked) when a scene starts or resumes, and a live conversation is paused when a check opens, resumes or restarts, so at most one is live; a parked check is not lost: home offers it as 'Carry on' (the existing check-part-way state) once the scene is finished or left. The 2026-09-25 owner decision is kept: with the TV on Linga home and a check left part-way, the phone still holds the check. Second, a check table in the shape of turn.ts: CHECK_STATES (about asked, reading, tasks between, say, listen, choose, verdict, plan asking the goal, plan topics, plan empty), ACCEPTS per state, checkAccepts and a refusal sentence. checkCommand asks the table once instead of its 8 stage guards, so plan-renew while the goal is asked, plan-add while the goal is asked and check-retry on the verdict are refused (409) instead of silently doing nothing or adding a topic no screen shows, and the view disables, from the same table, whatever the server would refuse.

## Flow
- Learner leaves the topic question, picks Booking from the menu: the check is parked, the phone shows Reply to Robin, the reply lands in the conversation.
- Learner finishes the rehearsal: home reads 'Find your level, you stopped part way: Carry on', and Carry on unparks the check where it was.
- Learner presses Find my level mid-scene: the scene pauses, the phone shows the check; Resume parks the check and the phone returns to the scene.
- Any client sending a check command the state does not take gets 409 and a sentence, and the view never drew that button enabled.

## Expected impact
Closes a path on which a reply is silently misfiled (a rehearsal reply stored as a goal, or scored as a level answer) and which the UAT run shows half the Characters can reach. Replaces 8 ad hoc guards and 3 unguarded commands with one table the server, the view and both devices share, so the next check feature (a second task kind, a plan-review step) is one row, as the next turn feature now is. The phone and the TV can no longer disagree about which activity is live.

## Evaluation
Claim: one ownerOf and one check table make the phone and TV agree on the live activity and make the server refuse exactly what the table refuses.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (cases 1-6 red; 7 and 8 are guards, green by design, so 0 of 6 behaviour cases)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/linga-rules-test.cjs, then npm test in desk/
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence:
Probe output (stub engine at the text() seam, scratch DESK_DATA_DIR, nothing under desk/data):
[A] level-self A2; plan-propose -> askGoal true, screen linga-plan, phonePanel check; check-leave -> check kept true, screen linga; start booking -> screen linga-talk, conversation turns 1, check stage plan, phonePanel check, answer {"action":"plan-goal","label":"Say what to practise"}; goal before '' , after the phone sends the view's answer 'Could you check my room, please?' -> preferences.goal 'Could you check my room, please?', conversation turns 1.
[B] start booking; check-start -> conversation paused false, check stage about, screen linga-check, phonePanel check; resume -> screen linga-talk, phonePanel check, check still true, answer check-answer.
[C] with askGoal true: plan-renew -> 200, no change, commands kept 0; plan-add 'football talk' -> topics 1, askGoal true.
Grep: s.check in desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts -> 0 code hits (one comment, line 189). Clearing a check: check.ts:214, check.ts:341-342, store.ts:451 only. Guards in check.ts: lines 61, 201, 229, 236, 241, 243, 267, 310, 323, 327, 331, 339 (stage or state guards: 201, 229, 236, 241, 267, 310, 323, 339 = 8).

title: One engine call core: a deadline and a typed error for every provider
body:
## Summary
Every engine call goes through one core that owns the deadline, the abort signal, the typed error and the provider/ms envelope. Today only text has a deadline you can set, five of the seven providers fail in ways the contract says they cannot, and the envelope is written four times.

## Description
The registry (registry.ts) and the shape rule (shape.ts) already made the engines one seam for WHICH provider runs and WHAT an answer must look like. They stopped short of HOW a call ends. A call ends one of three ways, and the engines implement each differently per provider:

- Deadline: claude kills its child on a timer (text.ts:59), codex does the same with a 240 s floor that overrides the caller (codex.ts:53), listen aborts a fetch (listen.ts:43), and four paths have none (vision.ts:28-31, embed.ts:18, voice.ts:46 Piper, voice.ts:67 ElevenLabs). Only TextRequest can carry timeoutMs (types.ts:12), so even a caller that wanted a vision or speech deadline could not say so.
- Failure: types.ts:6-7 promises a typed EngineError, but seven lines throw a plain Error or SyntaxError (voice.ts:49, 50, 53; vision.ts:33; embed.ts:21; listen.ts:46; codex.ts:62). job.ts:66 words a failure from EngineError.kind and drops to 'Try again.' for these, so the operator and the learner lose the reason.
- Success: the started/provider/run/name/ms envelope is written in answer() (shape.ts:96-102) and again, by hand, in embed(), listen() and speak().

Why this is the structural move and not tidying: a hung engine call is not a slow request, it is a stuck desk. runJob refuses a second run while the job is running (job.ts:76), the hint route and the TV key rule refuse the same way (hint/route.ts:28, keys.ts:195), retry only accepts a failed job (retry/route.ts:28), and a running job is settled only on restart (store.ts:202). So one vision stall in `read` leaves the page 'Reading' with no retry. The deadline belongs to the engine seam, once.

The move: a new call.ts exports `DEADLINE_MS` (per kind: text 90000, vision 180000, embed 60000, speak 30000, listen 120000), `deadlineFor(kind, provider, req)` (req.timeoutMs, else the kind's default, floored by an optional `Provider.deadlineMs` so codex keeps its 240000) and `call(kind, provider, req)`, which runs the provider with an AbortSignal, races it against the deadline, passes an EngineError through untouched, turns anything else into an EngineError of kind 'exit' with the first line of its message, and returns `{answer, provider, ms}`. answer() (text, vision, codexText), embed(), listen() and speak() each become a call to it. Providers drop their private timers and honour `ctx.signal`: the claude and codex children are killed on abort, the Ollama and ElevenLabs fetches get the signal, Piper's child is killed. VisionRequest, EmbedRequest, SpeakRequest and ListenRequest gain an optional timeoutMs.

Contract note (gate `contract`): `Provider.run(req, ctx?)` gains an optional second parameter and `Provider.deadlineMs?` is new; both are optional, so the 22 test files that stub run(req) are unaffected. Consumers of the changed behaviour: lib/desk/read.ts and mark.ts (vision), lib/library/lessons.ts (embed), api/speak and api/listen (routes keep their fixed 502 bodies), api/smoke, lib/desk/job.ts (kind -> sentence), tools/lab-bench.cjs and tools/calc-model-yield.cjs (wrappers that drop the second argument; the core still enforces the deadline).

## Flow
- A route or pipeline calls text(), vision(), embed(), speak() or listen() exactly as today.
- The engine function hands its provider and request to call(); the deadline is the request's timeoutMs, else the kind's default, floored by the provider's own.
- The provider runs with a signal. On the deadline the core aborts the signal and rejects with EngineError('timeout', providerName, ...); on a plain throw it rejects with EngineError('exit', ...) carrying the first line only.
- answer() still parses and validates; a shorten re-ask is a second call() with its own deadline, and if it hangs the first shape rejection stands.
- runJob receives a typed error in every case, so the job ends 'failed' with the desk's reason and the existing Try again path works.

## Expected impact
The desk can no longer be left waiting on a hung engine: every call ends in a typed result within a stated time, and the one place that states the times is a table in call.ts instead of three styles and four gaps. Piper, which has no timer at all today, stops being able to hold /api/speak and a child process forever. A new provider (Bedrock, Polly, named in four file headers as 'later') gets deadline, abort and error mapping by implementing run(), not by remembering to.

## Evaluation
Claim: every engine kind ends a call within its deadline with a typed EngineError, and the call envelope exists once.
Before: 0 of 5 acceptance cases pass (case 13 hangs for 5 of 5 kinds, case 15 fails for 5 of 5, plus the 4-of-7 and 7-site counts above)
After: 5 of 5 pass, plus 1 declared guard
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: types.ts:12 `export interface TextRequest { ...; timeoutMs?: number; ...}`; types.ts:13-16 VisionRequest, SpeakRequest, EmbedRequest, ListenRequest have no timeoutMs. grep -n 'timeoutMs' desk/src/lib/engines -> text.ts:59, codex.ts:53, types.ts:12 only. Deadlines: text.ts:59 `setTimeout(() => { child.kill(); reject(new EngineError('timeout', ...)) }, req.timeoutMs ?? 90000)`; codex.ts:53 `Math.max(req.timeoutMs ?? 90000, 240000)`; listen.ts:43 `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(120000)`; none at vision.ts:28 `fetch(`${HOST}/api/chat`, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(b) })`, embed.ts:18 `fetch(`${HOST}/api/embed`, ...)`, voice.ts:46 `spawn(PIPER, ['-m', PIPER_VOICE, '-f', out], { windowsHide: true })` with no timer, voice.ts:67 elevenlabs `fetch(...)`. Raw throws: voice.ts:49 `p.on('error', reject)`, voice.ts:50 `reject(new Error(`piper exited ${code}...`))`, voice.ts:53 `readFileSync(out)`, vision.ts:33 `await res.json()`, embed.ts:21 `await res.json()`, listen.ts:46 `(await r.json())`, codex.ts:62 `await readFile(last, 'utf8')`. Envelope copies: shape.ts:97-102, embed.ts:30-35, listen.ts:55-57, voice.ts:81-83 = 4. Stuck-job chain: job.ts:76 `if (now?.phase === 'running' && !opts.supersedes) return { ok: false, status: 409, error: BUSY }`; retry/route.ts:28 `job.phase !== 'failed'` -> 409 NOTHING; store.ts:202 settles running -> failed only inside load() of a saved session. Stubs: grep -l useProvider tools/*.cjs = 22 files; lab-bench.cjs:121 `async run(req) { const out = await inner.run(req);` and calc-model-yield.cjs:137 `run:async(req)=>{... inner.run(...)`. Earlier cards: challenge-2026-09-23 engines A (schema and registry, landed fe94a305) and B (jobs, landed) did not touch deadlines: shape.ts, registry.ts and job.ts say nothing of timeouts for vision, embed, speak or listen.

title: Stamp the product each run saw, so the open ledger says what is still true
body:
## Summary
OPEN.md says '186 open'. Every one of those rows was seen on a product in which 60 of the 63 files the driver loads have since changed, and the operator is not told. Stamp the product into every run, derive the same stamp from git for the old ones, and let OPEN.md and recertify.md say what is still seen on the current product, what is only old, and when a rerun's verdict change cannot be the product.

## Description
The overlay already records what instrument produced a run (model, efforts, screen cap, driver hashes) so that a driver change cannot pass for a product change. It never records the other half: which product the run exercised. The consequence is on the operator's screen today. uat/runs/OPEN.md reports 186 open rows in 36 pairs, drained 0 of 5, as if they were one backlog; the rows come from five runs committed on 15 Sep, and 135 commits to the files those runs loaded (60 of 63 changed) have landed since. Nothing separates a gap still present from one a later commit probably removed, and the only way to find out is the 36-pair recertify (about 30-50 model calls a pair). In the other direction, a recertify whose verdict drops on byte-identical product code is a measurement of judge and Character noise, but recertify.md has no way to say so and files it under Regressed.

The move: uat/driver/product.cjs derives the load set (the desk/src files in require.cache after the driver's entry modules load and one surface renders; no hand-kept list), stamps { commit, dirty, files: { path: blob sha } } into run.json beside instrument (never inside it, or a product change would read as an instrument confound), and answers seenOf(run) for a run without a stamp from git: the commit that first added the run's findings.json, with git ls-tree blobs compared to the working tree. The ledger gives each gap seen and changed; OPEN.md leads with the split and ends each row with 'product: N of 63 files changed since'. renderRecertify compares the two product stamps: identical means a verdict change is noise and is listed as confounded; different means it can be read as a product change and names the files. A run with neither stamp nor history is 'unknown', never current.

It asks for no new typing and no new run: it changes what the operator KNOWS from files and git already there. It is deliberately not a gap-to-file mapping (finding code_hint is empty on all 186 rows); it states a fact the repo can prove, product changed or not, and leaves attribution to the drain.

## Flow
- Operator runs `node uat/driver/linga-text.cjs --status`: OPEN.md opens with '186 open: 0 seen on the current product, 186 seen before a product change', each row ends with its own changed-file count.
- Operator runs any new run: run.json carries product; the next --status counts those rows as current until the product moves again.
- Operator runs a recertify: recertify.md says whether the product moved between the two runs; a drop on an unmoved product is shown as noise, a drop on a moved one as Regressed with the changed files named.

## Expected impact
The drain starts from an honest number: 186 rows become '0 current, 186 aged' instead of a flat backlog, and the first live run since 25 Sep (none exists on the verdict and instrument code) will be the first to give a current figure. Every future recertify becomes either a fix check or a free noise measurement, which the single-sample verdicts have lacked. Counted: 1 recorded fact added per run, 3 operator surfaces change (OPEN.md header, row suffix, recertify.md Confounded), 0 model calls added.

## Evaluation
Claim: the ledger and the recertify report state, from files and git alone, whether the product a finding was seen on has changed, and a verdict change on an unchanged product is reported as noise.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (cases 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7; cases 3 and 8 are guards, green before by design)
After: 6 of 6, guards still green
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: Run on HEAD fa6eb067 with a throwaway script: require surface.cjs install(), the nine entry modules of linga-text.cjs loadDesk()/child(), one surfaceOf(getSession()) -> 63 files of desk/src in require.cache. `git rev-parse f3542b5a:<file>` against `git hash-object <file>` over those 63: files 63, changed 60, new 0. `git log --since=2026-09-16 --oneline -- <63 files>` -> 135 commits; `-- desk/src` -> 192; `-- desk/src/lib/english desk/src/english` -> 38. ledger.ledger() over uat/runs: runs 5, rows 360, open 186, open rows with evidence[1] (code_hint) 0 of 186; run.json keys per run all null. First-add commits of findings.json: 0fa0af05 (lt, j1b), e4bfcfe9 (recert), f3542b5a (recert2-beginners, recert2-goal), all dated 2026-09-15. recertify.cjs:318-325 instrumentOf has no product field; recertify.cjs:143-145 flattens instrument, so a product map placed inside instrument would be reported as 'the instrument changed' and mask real regressions (renderRecertify whyNot(), :210).

title: The essay paragraph sits with its learner: no more guessing whose it is
body:
## Summary
One learner's Essay Master paragraph is on the next learner's TV. The landing and the recap each try to hide this with a guess. Make the paragraph travel with its learner, as Math Buddy's work already does, and both guesses go.

## Description
Math Buddy's work is seat-scoped: MathsSlot (store.ts:305) is swapped by seat() when a learner sits down, and late results go to the learner they belong to (toAway). Essay Master's paragraph, its chosen lens and the sentence it is on are not in the slot, and learner.set (store.ts:451) clears the conversation, the level check and the sentence analysis but not them. Reproduced: Ema's essay.set, then learner.set jakub, leaves state.essay set, and keys.lensStops then offers Jakub the 'last' card, which EssayTV draws as 'Last verdict' with Ema's summary.

The desk papered over it in two places with two different heuristics: landingRows.essayWaiting decides a paragraph is the learner's if their history holds a reading through a lens of that name, and recapRows.ownReading does the same with an extra condition. Both pass when the second learner has read the same lens, so the very case they exist for is the one they miss. A reading that finishes after a switch has the same flaw in the other direction: analyse/route.ts dispatches essay.set with no owner.

The move: essay, essayType and essayAt join the slot, so seating a learner swaps them like a practice set; essay.type and essay.set take an optional owner, the route stamps it from the learner who asked, and an owner who is no longer at the desk gets the reading in away[owner] without the TV being sent to their forensic page. The two heuristics then read s.essay and nothing else.

## Flow
- Ema reads a paragraph through the Argument lens; the TV goes to her forensic page.
- She picks Someone else and chooses Jakub: the paragraph goes into away.ema, Jakub's Essay Master home has four lenses and no 'last' card, and the landing's Essay Master card is his own reading or two words.
- Ema comes back: her paragraph, lens and sentence are where she left them.
- Ema asks for a reading, the desk is handed to Jakub while it thinks: the reading lands in away.ema, the TV stays on the landing, nothing of hers appears for him.

## Expected impact
A shared family desk (Family Phase 1 puts two learners on one TV) stops showing one child's essay verdict to another, on the lens home, the landing card and the recap. Two copies of an ownership heuristic become none, so the next screen that reads the paragraph (the phone, a week digest) cannot get it wrong. The persisted session gains three optional keys per away slot and nothing else.

## Evaluation
Claim: Essay Master's paragraph is seat-scoped like Math Buddy's work, and no consumer needs a heuristic to know whose it is.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass for the cases that are not GUARDs (cases 1-4, 6-8 fail; case 5 is a GUARD, green by design)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: Reproduction run in-process with the repo's own loader (store.fresh(), learner ema, reduce essay.set, reduce learner.set jakub, DESK_DATA_DIR in the OS temp dir): output `learner jakub essay kept: true essayType null lensStops last: true`. Sites that decide ownership of s.essay: landingRows.ts:143-146 (label match), recapRows.ts:148-152 (label match plus sentences), keys.ts:110 and EssayTV.tsx:112-114 (no test at all) = 4 sites, 3 behaviours. Fields outside the seat swap: store.ts:230 essay, essayType; essayAt (3 fields) against 13 in MathsSlot. Events that write the paragraph with no owner: essay.type, essay.set (store.ts:496-498) from one route call (analyse/route.ts:54-56) that awaits a model call between them; events that already carry owner for the same reason: hint.stage, practice.marked, page.read, hint.set, lesson.set (5). The essay-master rider scout may reach the lens-home half of this; the landing half (two guards that retire) is why it is filed here.

title: A relay socket is not a pen: the pen conversation follows the pen, not the channel
body:
## Summary
Over the relay the TV closes its own socket 5 seconds after it dials, a phone's single hello is lost whenever it lands in the resulting gap, and a second phone is never PIN-checked at all. All three come from one assumption: that a channel carries exactly one pen. LAN does; the relay does not.

## Description
The pen conversation (PenConversation) is created once per channel and its hello timeout is armed when the channel opens. On the LAN transport a channel is a phone, so that is right. On the relay transport a channel is the TV's single outbound socket, which exists before any phone and outlives each one. Three things follow, none of which a test sees because relay-test.mjs pairs inside the first window:

1. The hello deadline fires on an empty socket. PenSessionHost.kt:61-65 carries out PenConversation's reject, and channel.close() hangs up on the relay. RelayTransport then backs off because a 5 s connection is never healthy (HEALTHY_MS is 10 s): 1, 2, 4, 8, 10 s gaps. The TV is deaf for 10 of every 15 s in steady state, and the companion sends hello once (index.html:175), so a phone that arrives in a gap never pairs and is told nothing.
2. A later phone (or the same phone after a drop) sends a second Hello into an already-paired conversation. PenConversation.kt:107-111 delivers it as input and PenEngine ignores it: no PIN check, no Welcome, strokes accepted. The PIN, which the relay design says is the only guard because the relay stays dumb (RelayTransport.kt:28-29), stops guarding after the first pairing.
3. The bookkeeping that a Paired effect triggers (count, heartbeat ticker) assumes one Paired per conversation.

The move is to make 'does this channel carry one pen' a property the conversation knows. PenChannel gets `carriesOnePen` (LAN true, relay false). PenConversation, opened as shared, has no hello deadline and treats every Hello as a (re)pairing: right PIN -> Welcome + Paired(replaced = true) at a new generation; wrong PIN -> Welcome(refused), an Unpaired effect, and input dropped until a right hello, with no Close because closing would hang up on the relay. Dedicated conversations (LAN) are byte-for-byte what they are today, pinned by the existing cases. PenSessionHost cancels the previous ticker on a replaced Paired (a fresh Heartbeat is exactly what a new phone needs to receive the document and thumbnail again) and counts one pen per conversation. The wire shape does not change; a Welcome may now arrive mid-stream, which companion/index.html:192-207 already handles.

## Flow
- TV dials the relay; nothing happens for a minute; the socket stays open (today it is closed at 5 s)
- viewer scans the QR 40 s later; hello arrives; Welcome + Paired; heartbeat starts
- phone 1 leaves, phone 2 loads the page with the PIN; hello is re-evaluated; right PIN pairs, wrong PIN is refused and the phone shows its PIN box
- an intruder's wrong-PIN hello unpairs the current pen instead of riding on its pairing

## Expected impact
The relay, which docs/PLATFORM-RISK.md calls mandatory on a Vega port, becomes pairable at any time instead of one second in three, a reconnecting phone gets its Welcome, and the PIN guards every pen rather than the first. LAN behaviour is pinned unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: a shared (relay) conversation pairs at any time, re-pairs every hello, refuses a wrong PIN without hanging up, and a dedicated (LAN) conversation is unchanged
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard acceptance cases pass (the `shared` parameter and Unpaired do not exist; the observable defects are counted in the premise: 1 deadline armed at socket open, 10 s of every 15 s deaf, 0 Welcomes to a second hello)
After: 7 of 7 (6 JUnit, 1 operator-run device case)
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: grep -rn 'onPen(' tv-app -> LanTransport.kt:111 (per phone connection) and RelayTransport.kt:56 (per TV socket): 2 sites, different lifetimes, one conversation model. grep -n 'desk.open' -> PenSessionHost.kt:40 (inside host(), so at channel open). grep -n 'HELLO_TIMEOUT_MS' -> PenConversation.kt:50, PenSessionHost.kt:62. RelayTransport.kt:81-83: INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS = 500, MAX_BACKOFF_MS = 10_000, HEALTHY_MS = 10_000; a 5 s socket takes the `else` branch at :65-66, so gaps are 1,2,4,8,10,10 s and the TV's open windows are 0-5, 6-11, 13-18, 22-27, 35-40, 50-55, 65-70 s (5 s open per 15 s at the cap). PenConversation.kt:93 `if (hello == null) {` is the only place PIN is compared (:95); lines :107-111 are the path a second Hello takes; PenEngine.kt:111 `is PenMessage.Hello, is PenMessage.Transport, is PenMessage.Ping -> Unit`. tools/relay-stub.mjs:103 `if (other && other.readyState === other.OPEN) other.send(text);` (no else). companion/index.html:173-176 `ws.onopen = () => { connected = true; send({ type: 'hello', pin, clientId }); };` is the only hello site. tools/relay-test.mjs:157-196 dials, reads logcat, launches chromium, and expects pairing inside one run with no case for a late or second phone.

title: The certificate shows what it still needs, and the next scene steers toward it
body:
## Summary
A Linga learner works toward a certificate the desk never shows them. They finish a whole plan, home says 'Every topic talked through', and no certificate arrives, because two of the six skills a B1 certificate asks for were never in any topic. Nothing on any screen says what is missing, and 'Talk again' starts the first topic over. A learner who picked their level by hand can never be issued one at all and is never told. The desk already holds everything needed: what the band requires, what has been shown, what has not.

## Description
The certificate (W10) is issued by code when every required skill is 'on your own' and the latest record is a level check with medium or high confidence. The requirement is the band's base skills (cert.ts:35-52) widened by the skills of the agreed plan's topics (cert.ts:76-80). Three things leave the learner blind. One: a plan is only asked to span four skills (check.ts:159) while B1 needs six, and a scene records evidence only for its own focus skill, its review skill and repair (conversation.ts:218), so a certificate is reachable only if the plan or the learner's own situation choice happens to cover the rest. Two: recommendScene (curriculum.ts:83-110) never reads the requirement, so the 'next topic' and 'Talk again' ignore it. Three: the certificate surface does not exist until one is issued (view.ts:350-352 and 433), and a hand-picked band, which never certifies (cert.ts:68), says nothing.

The move has one pure function and three places that read it. certGap(learning) in cert.ts returns the band, which required skills are shown (with spoken or written, from the same evidence the plate uses), which are open, and the blocker when none can be issued (a hand-picked band, a low-confidence check, no check). Then: (1) recommendScene prefers, once the unstarted plan topics are done, a plan topic or built-in situation that practises an open skill, so 'Talk again' and the phone's Next topic lead somewhere; unstarted plan topics still lead first. (2) The TV's certificate screen, which today is a 'No certificate yet' page, becomes the plate in outline: the band and its name, the skills already shown as on the issued plate, and the open ones as dashed empty slots, in the Open Door's own dashed-path grammar (the Stones), with no number anywhere. A hand-picked band shows the plate without slots and one caption sentence, with Find my level as its action. (3) The menu door 'My certificate' appears for any learner with a record of checks, not only after one is issued. The picture is the verdict; the caption is one sentence of under 25 words. The TV never asks for typing and puts no answer on screen: it names skills, never a quote or a phrase to say.

## Flow
- Learner finishes the last plan topic. Home: 'Every topic talked through'; Talk again now starts Understand and repair, the first open skill, not the first topic.
- Menu, My certificate: the B1 plate in outline, four skills filled (spoken, written), two dashed slots; caption 'Each empty slot is a conversation still to have.'
- Learner whose level was picked by hand opens it: the plate with no slots, 'A certificate rests on a level check you take with Linga', and Find my level.
- The certificate issues as today when the last slot fills; the outline becomes the plate with its quote.

## Expected impact
Turns the reward from a surprise that may never come into a path the learner can see and walk, with no score and no count. Makes the end of a plan lead to the skills a certificate lacks instead of repeating the first topic, and tells a hand-picked learner the truth once instead of never. The data (placements, plan, evidence, achievements) is already on the record; no stored shape changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: certGap derives what a certificate still needs; recommendScene, the certificate screen and the menu act on it, and the plate stays free of digits, counts and game words.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (cases 1-3 and 5-7 red; case 4 is a guard and case 8 is the operator capture)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/cert-rules-test.cjs, then npm test in desk/, then the Playwright capture
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
Probe (scratch data dir, no engine; B1 learner, check medium confidence, plan topics over contact, request, describe, narrate, describe, request, all six started, eight independent typed pieces over those four skills):
required contact,repair,request,describe,narrate,negotiate
progress {contact:independent, repair:not-tried, request:independent, describe:independent, narrate:independent, negotiate:not-tried, relate:not-tried, resolve:not-tried}
issue null
planDone true
recommended next skill contact plan-0
grep 'cert' in desk/src/lib/english/curriculum.ts -> false
after a hand-picked B1 appended to the record -> certBand null
Lines: cert.ts:35-52 (BASE_SKILLS), 66-69 (certBand), 76-80 (requirementFor), 114-130 (issue); check.ts:159 ('at least four different skills'); conversation.ts:218 (skills observed per turn); curriculum.ts:83-110; view.ts:277, 350-352, 433; cert-rules-test.cjs:395-396; linga-cert-live.cjs:8. The record of checks: grep placements in desk/src -> cert.ts, check.ts, conversation.ts, rules.ts, types.ts, placement.ts only; no view, no TV or phone component.

title: The pairing card knows whether a pen is holding it, and gives the picture back
body:
## Summary
The TV's only interface is a white card parked on the picture forever that cannot tell a waiting TV from a paired one. Make the card follow the pen: invite while no pen is here, a dot once one is, the QR back when it is lost, and the reason when it is refused.

## Description
A telestrator exists to put ink on a picture, and today 11% of that picture belongs to the pairing card for the whole session (the harness itself excludes the region, live-ui-test.mjs:53-54). The TV already holds every fact that would let the card step aside: Paired and close happen in PenSessionHost, a refusal is a PenEffect.Close, the transport reports its failure. None of it reaches the screen, because the pen count is an AtomicInteger nothing observes.

The move is a small sans-IO state in core, LinkState, with a reducer over events (Ready, Failed, PenPaired, PenGone, PenRefused, Peek) and a view(nowMs) that returns what the corner should show: Connecting, Invite (QR plus the PIN as large digits), Chip (a dot, nothing else), Lost (QR back after a 3 s grace), Refused (two words, 5 s), Failed (the reason, large). It is JVM-tested on a clock the test passes in, exactly like PenConversation. tv-app only feeds it events and renders it: PenSessionHost forwards Paired, close and refusals, Session exposes a StateFlow, and a new PairingCard.kt draws each view with strings from strings.xml. The URL is stored in the state on Ready instead of being polled at 30 Hz from a composable. A stale close from a superseded pen is ignored by client id, which is also the correct 'who is current' fact the open /health pens item is missing. Menu on the remote peeks the card (and the status line) for 8 s, so a second phone can still be paired; the remote already has no use for that key.

The QR carries the PIN, so the TV never asks for typing. The PIN is shown as digits only in Invite and Refused, which is the one moment a viewer has to type it on the phone after a refusal (the phone page already says 'type the PIN from the TV').

## Flow
- launch: card in the corner, QR and four large PIN digits
- scan: the card collapses to a dot within a frame; the picture is clean
- phone drops out of Wi-Fi: after 3 s the card returns with 'Pen lost' and the same QR; re-pair and it collapses again
- a neighbour guesses a wrong PIN while someone is drawing: nothing covers the picture
- no pen yet and a wrong PIN: the card says 'Wrong PIN' in two words, then goes back to inviting
- Menu: card and status line for 8 s, then gone

## Expected impact
The viewer gets the full picture while drawing, the person at the TV knows whether the phone is holding the pen, a failed pairing says why in a size that reads from a sofa, and a poll per frame leaves the draw path. No wire, no engine, no overlay change.

## Evaluation
Claim: the corner of the picture is occupied only when a pen is needed or lost, and every state is decided in code, not in a composable
Before: 0 of 7 non-guard acceptance cases pass (LinkState does not exist); 1 view (always-on card) for 6 situations; 3 text lines at 10-11sp; 1 pairingUrl() poll per frame
After: 8 of 8 (8 JUnit; compile gate plus an emulator capture operator-run)
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: MainActivity.kt:225-230 `PairingCard(url = transport.pairingUrl() ?: "connecting…", transport = transport.name, failure = transportFailure, modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.TopEnd).padding(24.dp))` with no condition around it. grep -rn 'connectedPens\|penConnected\|penDisconnected' tv-app core -> Health.kt:21, PenSessionHost.kt:54, :77, Session.kt:44, :55, :57: the count never reaches Compose. tools/live-ui-test.mjs:54 `if (x > width * 0.74 && y < height * 0.44) continue;` is the card's footprint, 11.4% of the screen. MainActivity.kt:266 `fontSize = 11.sp`, :267 `fontSize = 10.sp`, :269 `fontSize = 10.sp` (the red failure line). MainActivity.kt:164-174 loop writes tMs every delay(33); :234 reads it in the body, so the scope recomposes and :226 re-evaluates pairingUrl(), which LanTransport.kt:143-146 answers with NetworkInterface.getNetworkInterfaces() each time. PenSessionHost.kt:48-51 `is PenEffect.Close -> { Log.i(TAG, "pen rejected via ${channel.remoteName}: ${effect.reason}") ...`. MainActivity.kt:124-132: 9 key codes handled, KEYCODE_MENU not among them.

title: One item kind: the marker, the explainer and the hint read the same registry
body:
## Summary
Math Buddy decides what KIND of item it is looking at (a linear equation the model wrote, a Calculus spec, a school unit's spec) by three different mechanisms at 15 lines in 7 files, and four marking loops carry the same scaffold. One registry (`rules/kinds.ts`) and one pure judge replace them: a sheet is read by the model, judged per item in code, and recorded once.

## Description
The decision that is the product (is this answer right, which slip, what may the desk say) is made by whichever file asks, in its own way. The photo path chooses a marker for the whole sheet (`mark.ts:158-159`), the typed path chooses per item (`mark.ts:328`), the explainer re-detects from the item (`explain.ts:196`), the hint chooses its stance from the learner's path (`hint.ts:57-58`) but its leak check and fallback line from the question's text (`hint.ts:65,77,106`), the generator from the topic (`items.ts:123-124`).

The cost is visible two ways. First, behaviour: probed on the current tree, the same three strings on the same mixed sheet are marked right, wrong, right when typed and right, wrong, unsure when photographed; a school-path learner's derivative question gets the linear-equations stance ('factoring and linear-equations unit; prefer the unit's methods over heavier ones') while its leak check already reads it as Calculus; a Calculus-path learner's fractions task gets the Calculus I stance. Second, change cost: a fourth kind (or the Phase 2 placement staircase, which judges single items of many kinds with no practice set, `mathsRows.ts:55`) means editing 7 files, copying a fifth marking loop and re-deciding the kind by a fourth mechanism.

The move: `rules/kinds.ts` holds `kindOfSpec(spec)`, `kindOfQuestion(text)` and `kindOfTopic(topicId)` (all pure, built on the existing `isCalcSpec`, `isSchoolSpec`, the two `specFromQuestion` readers and `pathOfTopic`), and `judgeItem(item, read, ctx)` / `judgeSet(practice, reads, ctx)`, the one decision. `mark.ts` keeps the model half (three reading prompts and schemas, unchanged) and returns `Read[]`; `judgeSet` settles each item by ITS kind; `markTyped` builds its reads from the typed strings; `land()` is called once. A linear read that carries the model's own solution keeps today's rule (the solution must hold, else the desk asks); a linear read with no solution field is judged by the code's own root (`rootOf`, not degenerate), which is exactly what typed marking does today. The explainer's spoken-value settle (`settle`) stays as it is; only its kind detection and leak dispatch move onto the registry. The hint's stance follows the item's kind where the text reads, and falls back to the learner's path only where it does not; the voice stays the learner's.

## Flow
- Phone photographs or types -> `/api/mark` -> `markSet` (reader by sheet kind, unchanged prompts) or `markTyped` -> `judgeSet` -> `land` -> `practice.marked`: nothing the TV or the phone sees changes shape.
- Homework hint -> `kindOfQuestion(item.text)` picks stance, leak rule, unit name and withheld line from one answer; `api/hint` asks the same function for the lesson library.
- `makeItems` -> `kindOfTopic` replaces the two inline `pathOfTopic` tests.
- Future: a placement item is `judgeItem` with a spec and an answer, no sheet.

## Expected impact
Four marking loops become one judge plus three readers (mark.ts 372 lines to roughly 240); the kind is decided by one module instead of 15 lines in 7 files; typed and photographed marking of the same strings cannot disagree for any mix of kinds, which today is pinned for school sets only; two real prompt mismatches in the hint close; and the Phase 2 placement staircase and card B's second go get a single-item entry point instead of a private function.

## Evaluation
Claim: one registry and one pure judge make marking, explaining and hinting agree on an item's kind, closing a typed-versus-photo disagreement and a hint-stance mismatch that probes show today, without changing any screen or stored shape.
Before: 0 of 7 behaviour cases pass (case 6 is a declared GUARD, green before by design); probe: typed marks a mixed sheet right, wrong, right and photo marks it right, wrong, unsure; mark.ts has 4 loops, 4 land() calls, 3 byN maps, 4 unsure++ sites.
After: 7 of 7 behaviour cases pass and the guard stays green; school-marking, calc-marking, calc-hint, maths-rules, school-stretch suites unchanged and green; 1 land() call in mark.ts.
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: probe (scratch node script on HEAD fa6eb067, desk's own typescript, vision stub): mixed practice [{n:1 school compute 3/4 + 1/6 spec}, {n:2 calc derivative f x^2 spec}, {n:3 'x+3=7' no spec}], answers 11/12, 3x, 4 -> markTyped(...).items = [1 right],[2 wrong],[3 right]; markSet('img', ...) with the stub reading the same strings = [1 right],[2 wrong],[3 unsure]. probe 2 (engines/text stub, hint('maths', q, {path, age:13}).system): path school + 'Find the derivative of x^2 + 3x' -> 'You are a maths tutor for a learner aged 11 to 13. This sheet is a factoring and linear-equations unit; prefer the unit's methods over heavier ones.'; path calc1 + 'Work out 3/4 - 1/6' -> 'You are a maths tutor for a first-year university student in Calculus I. Use the course's methods ...'; path school + 'Work out 3/4 - 1/6' -> 'This sheet is the unit "Add and subtract fractions"' (so the unit stance exists and is suppressed only by the learner's path). probe 3: of 960 school-generated questions (every unit with a generator, seeds 1-40, tiers 1-2) calc.specFromQuestion reads 0 and school.specFromQuestion reads 960 (the readers do not overlap, so kind-by-text is safe). grep: mark.ts byN at 177,225,259; unsure++ at 197,238,271,314; attempts.push at 206,241,274,317; return land( at 212,246,278,320; the return-type literal 'items: PracticeItem[]; provider: string; ms: number; unsure: number; landed: boolean' 5 times. Kind-deciding lines: items.ts:123,124; rules/maths.ts:78,142,147; hint.ts:58,76,77; api/hint/route.ts:51; mark.ts:158,159,328; explain.ts:196; store.ts:143,148 = 15 lines in 7 files. Never-re-propose check: challenge-2026-09-25 desk-pipelines A moved slip location into rules/maths (locate) and challenge-2026-09-23 desk-pipelines A built the job runner; neither unified the kind. Shared hot files avoided: store.ts, tv/keys.ts, tv/screens.tsx, uat/driver/linga-text.cjs are not in the write set.

title: Engine check answers in seconds: what would run, whether it answers, what to fix
body:
## Summary
The Engine check link on the desk landing page (app/page.tsx:16) becomes a status the operator can read at a glance. It lists all five engines with the provider that would run, whether it answers and what to do when it does not, in about two seconds and with no model call. A `?live=1` run does the real calls in parallel.

## Description
The route's own comment says its job: 'a broken engine is found here and not on the TV' (smoke/route.ts:1). It does that job slowly and partially. It runs the text, embed and vision calls in series (route.ts:14-20), so the answer arrives after the sum of the slowest three. It covers 3 of the 5 engines, mislabels a Piper-only desk as 'key present' (route.ts:12), omits listen although listenStatus() exists (listen.ts:27), never says which provider is active although activeProvider() was written for exactly that (registry.ts:36) and nothing in desk/src calls it, and on failure prints the engine's own message (route.ts:13), the class of leak 4772d195 closed on the speech routes. A paired phone, not only the TV, can start the three model calls, because the route never reads the role.

The operator's real questions are cheap to answer from facts the desk already holds: which provider would run, is its binary or host reachable, is the model pulled, is the key or the voice file there. Those need a probe, not a model call.

The move: an optional `Provider.probe(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; say: string }>` (types.ts) implemented by each provider in one or two lines of real checking: claude-cli resolves its binary, codex resolves its launcher (codex.ts launcher()), the two Ollama engines GET /api/tags and look for their model (so a missing model says 'ollama pull qwen3.8:27b' and an unreachable host says 'ollama serve' with the host), Piper checks its two paths, ElevenLabs checks the key is set without calling it, listen reuses listenStatus(). A new `health.ts` exports `engineStatus(budgetMs)`, which asks each kind's ACTIVE provider (activeProvider) for its probe in parallel under a budget and returns rows `{ kind, provider, ok: boolean | null, say, ms }` (null when a provider has no probe, never a guess), and `engineCheck({ live, sample })`, which for `live` also runs text, vision (when a sample page exists), embed and speak in parallel and reports the engine's own provider and ms, with failures as `{ kind, say }` from the EngineError kind and the detail sent to console.error as job.ts does. The route returns those rows, runs live only on `?live=1`, and answers a phone 403 (the TV, or an in-process caller with no role header, may ask).

Contract note (gate `contract`): the route's response shape changes. Its consumers: app/page.tsx:16 (a plain link, no parse), desk/README.md:30 (prose, updated here), no script or test reads it today (grep above). The 403 for a paired phone tightens who may start model calls; it does not open any route to a guest, so the pairing rule in proxy.ts is untouched.

## Flow
- The operator opens Engine check from the TV's browser: five rows appear at once, e.g. text claude-cli ok, vision ollama NOT ok 'ollama pull qwen3.8:27b', embed ollama ok, speak piper ok, listen gravitone ok.
- A row that is not ok says what to do in one line.
- To prove a path end to end, the operator adds ?live=1: the real calls run side by side and each row reports its provider and milliseconds.
- A paired phone that loads the same address gets 403 and no engine is touched.

## Expected impact
The first thing an operator does when a page read or a hint fails is open this check; today that is a wait of up to a couple of minutes for a JSON dump that skips listen, mislabels Piper and names no provider. After the change the same question takes two seconds, covers all five engines, and the commonest failures (Ollama down, model not pulled, no CLI, no key, STT not running) each read as an instruction. A child's phone can no longer spend model calls by loading a URL.

## Evaluation
Claim: the engine check reports all five engines with their active provider and a fix line in one parallel round, without a model call, and a phone cannot start the live run.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (the route runs 3 live calls in series, covers 3 of 5 engines, has no probe, no role check and no test)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: smoke/route.ts:12 `const out = { voice: voiceConfigured() ? 'key present' : 'no key' };` route.ts:13 `out[name] = { error: String(e).slice(0, 300) }`; route.ts:14 `await t('text', ...)`, :15 `await t('embed', ...)`, :16 `await t('vision', ...)` - three awaits in series; nothing for listen. voice.ts:38 `export function voiceConfigured() { return piperReady() || Boolean(KEY); }`. registry.ts:36 `export function activeProvider(kind: EngineKind): string` ('Starts nothing', :35); grep -rn activeProvider desk/src -> registry.ts:36 and :48 only; tools: engines-rules-test.cjs:86-89, lab-bench.cjs:185. listen.ts:27 `export async function listenStatus()` reached only from api/listen/route.ts:5. proxy.ts:29 `if (role === 'guest' && !OPEN[...]?.includes(req.method)) return 401` - tv and phone both pass; smoke route has no role read (pairing.ts:82 roleFrom is unused there). grep -rln 'api/smoke' tools uat desk/src -> app/api/smoke/route.ts, app/page.tsx only (0 tests). Commit 4772d195 message: 'both speech routes echoed the engine's own error, which can carry a key fragment'. vision.ts:16 `qwen3.8:27b`, :32 `ollama ${res.status}: ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 300)}`; embed.ts:12 `nomic-embed-text`. Prior cards: no challenge card or finding in challenge-2026-09-23/25, backlog, followup or optimize-2026-09-30 runs touches /api/smoke or engine health (findings titles listed and checked).

title: Continue as Ema continues: Select opens what is waiting, not the app's home
body:
## Summary
The landing says 'Continue as Ema' and then opens Math Buddy's front door. Make Select open the thing that is waiting: the marked sheet, the set on paper, the snapped page, the paragraph Ema was reading.

## Description
The desk already knows what each app has waiting (landingRows.deskWaiting) and the caption already names it ('Two-step equations, 3 of 4 right. The marked set is still on the desk.'). Select ignores that and opens MODULE_HOME: Math Buddy's Tonight, where the first stop is a continue card for the same set and a second Select opens it; Essay Master's lens home with the lamp on the first lens, not the lens Ema read. Recap's Select and Tonight's continue card both already know how to open the waiting thing, in two copies of the same branch; the landing is the one place that has the answer on screen and does not use it.

The move is one helper in keys.ts, openWaiting(s, app), that returns the events for an app's waiting thing: Math Buddy through continueCard (sheet, practice or page), Essay Master to the forensic page when the paragraph on the desk is the learner's, otherwise to the lens home with the lamp on the lens last read, and everything else (nothing waiting, Linga, whose home leads with its own Carry on) to the home as today. The landing, Tonight's continue card and the recap all call it, so there is one place that says what resuming means. No new words on the TV: the caption already carries the sentence.

## Flow
- Ema comes back to a marked set. The lamp rests on Math Buddy; the caption says it is still on the desk. Select: the hand-off plays and the sheet opens on the first slip. Back is Tonight, then the desk.
- Ema was reading the Argument lens. Select on Essay Master opens her paragraph's forensic page, or, with no paragraph in the session, the lens home with the lamp on Argument.
- Nothing is waiting, or the app is Linga: Select opens the front door exactly as before.

## Expected impact
The most common return path (the landing to the thing you left) loses one screen and one press for Math Buddy, and Essay Master stops dropping the learner on the wrong lens. The label 'Continue as Ema' becomes true. Three copies of 'open what an app has waiting' become one with a test that pins them equal, so a later change to Tonight's continue card cannot make the landing and the recap disagree.

## Evaluation
Claim: Select on the app in the light opens what the caption says is waiting, through one helper that Tonight and the recap share.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass for the non-GUARD cases (cases 1-6 and 8 fail; case 7 is a GUARD, green by design)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first, plus one live journey
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: keys.ts:226 `o.ev({ type: "subject", subject: at }); o.nav(MODULE_HOME[at]);` against keys.ts:241-246 and keys.ts:413-425 (two copies of the real open: `if (cont?.go === "page") { o.ev({ type: "page.select", ... }); o.nav("page"); } else if (cont) o.nav(cont.go, cont.focus);`) = 3 handlers, 1 that does not use the data. Presses from the landing to the marked sheet today: 2 Selects across 2 screens (landing, tonight, sheet); after: 1. tv-keys-test.cjs:349 pins `{type:'nav',screen:'essaytype',focus:0}` for a desk whose only waiting item is an Argument reading (readIt, line 291; ESSAY_TYPES order structure, argument, evidence, language puts Argument at index 1). The map description (context-map.json landing) names 'continue' and the lamp resting on what was left, so the card is inside the context's scope; the session event shapes, routes and persisted JSON are unchanged, hence gate none.

title: One metric registry that the judge schema, gates, roll-up and report all read
body:
## Summary
The set of metrics a Linga journey is judged on is written out five times in uat/driver, and the copies already disagree. Make one registry the only place a metric is declared; the judge schema, the gates, the roll-up, the before/after delta and the report are derived from it.

## Description
The verdict, ledger and recertify work moved the decision into code, and in doing so each module re-listed the metrics it needs. The judge is asked for five metric groups (linga-text.cjs:76-82). verdict.cjs can gate six series (:71-78) and cannot gate judge agreement. recertify.cjs rolls up and deltas seven (:53-77). The report prints six bullets (:313-318). Moment recall is asked, stored, and read by nothing. Check length is in the rubric and in J1's measures list and exists nowhere in code. A gate with a typo is found only after the run.

The move is a new uat/driver/metrics.cjs: each entry declares its judge key, the JSON schema of that key, and its series (id, label, an of(record) that returns [numerator, denominator], and how a gate reads it). placement stays special only in that its of() reads record.facts.placement.class. linga-text.cjs builds the metrics half of judgeSchema from the registry; verdict.cjs gateReason() reads series by id; recertify.cjs rollUp() and metricDelta() fold over series; synthesize() and characterReport() print one line per series. A journey's gates are validated against the registry when the runner starts. The judge schema stays byte-identical for the existing metrics (case 1 pins it), so no prompt, finding or committed run changes; the one visible change is that moment recall is finally reported.

A second module's metric (Math Buddy's hint withholding, marking agreement) then becomes one registry entry instead of five edits across three files.

## Flow
- Operator adds a metric: one entry in metrics.cjs and, if it should gate, one line in a journey's gates.
- Run start: unknownGates() checks every journey file; a typo stops the run before any model call.
- Judge answers, verdictOf() gates it, rollUp()/metricDelta() track it across reruns, report.md prints it. No other edit.

## Expected impact
Operators: a verdict, a delta and a report row can no longer disagree about what a metric is, and a metric the rubric promises (recall) shows up. Builders: the next module's UAT is a registry entry, not a five-file hunt. Counted: 5 hand-kept lists collapse to 1, 1 asked-but-unread metric becomes read, 1 rubric metric with no code is named as driver-measured instead of silently absent.

## Evaluation
Claim: the metric set is declared once, and the schema, gates, roll-up, delta and report are derived from it without changing any existing output.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (cases 2-7; cases 1 and 8 are guards, green before by design)
After: 6 of 6, guards still green
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
